title: Aggrega Background Daemon Wire Protocol
description: The message shapes exchanged with a background compiler daemon started by `aggrega serve`. A client opens a session over that daemon with the handshake, and the session is what scopes the settings and the workspace the conversation was opened over; the daemon is the process that answers a request, sends a notification and holds what it has read. The protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0 over standard input and output, each message framed by a Content-Length header; this document describes the message bodies and neither the framing nor the transport. A body is one of four things: a request the client sends, a notification the client sends, a notification the daemon sends, or the response the daemon returns for a request. Three properties of the surface decide how the shapes below are written. First, every request admits two fields beyond the ones its own method declares — `workspaceRoot`, naming the workspace the request acts on, and `workDoneToken`, the caller-minted value progress is reported under — so both appear on every request params object here, including the three methods whose subject is not a workspace: `aggrega/getSchema` and `aggrega/scaffoldEntity` accept `workspaceRoot` and ignore it, and `aggrega/initialize` reads it as the workspace the session declares. Second, the daemon refuses a request params object carrying a field the method does not accept, naming what it does accept, so every params object here is closed at its top level; a nested object inside a request is not closed, because the check reads only the outermost field names. Third, a result is composed by the daemon rather than supplied by a caller, so result objects are closed at every level whose shape is fixed, and open only where the value is opaque JSON the daemon carries through without reading. One consequence of the daemon's encoding is visible on the wire and is described rather than tidied away: a collection the daemon does not mark optional is emitted as `null` when it has no value to report and as an empty collection when the value it reports is empty, so both forms are admitted wherever that applies.

ProtocolVersion.description: The JSON-RPC version every message carries. Only 2.0 is spoken.

RequestId.description: The caller's identifier for a request, echoed on the response that answers it. A message carrying no identifier is a notification and is never answered.

ProgressToken.description: A value the caller mints so it can match progress notifications to the call that asked for them. It is echoed back on every notification unchanged, so a caller may compare it to the value it sent. It is accepted on every request, and a request that sends one in a session which declared no progress capability is refused.
ProgressToken.x-aggrega-wire-note: carried through unparsed so the bytes a caller matches on are never perturbed

WorkspaceRootSubject.description: The absolute path of the workspace this request acts on. It is the request's subject: the daemon resolves it before the method runs, and a request that omits it or spells it as anything other than a string is refused.

WorkspaceRootAccepted.description: The absolute path of a workspace. This method's subject is not a workspace — it answers from what the binary itself carries — so the field is accepted and not read. It is admitted because a client may send it uniformly on every request without having to know which methods consult it.

RequestMethod.description: Every method a request may name. The set is closed: a request naming anything else is answered with a method-not-found error.

ClientNotificationMethod.description: Every method a client notification may name. The set is closed, and neither notification is answered.

DaemonNotificationMethod.description: Every method a notification the daemon sends may name. The set is closed.

Request.description: A request the client sends and the daemon answers. The method names what is being asked; the params object carries that method's own fields plus the two every method admits. A request that omits params entirely is read as one whose fields are all absent.

ClientNotification.description: A notification the client sends. It carries no identifier and is never answered.

DaemonNotification.description: A notification the daemon sends. It carries no identifier and is never answered.

CancelRequestParams.description: Asks the daemon to abandon a request already in flight, naming it by the identifier the request carried. A request already finished, or never sent, is silently nothing to cancel.

ShutdownParams.description: Asks the daemon to stop accepting work and finish what it has already taken. The notification carries no fields, and the notification itself is usually sent with no params object at all. A second one abandons the work still in flight instead of waiting for it.

ProgressParams.description: One report of work in progress, sent only for a request that minted a progress token in a session that declared it could receive them.

value.description: The report itself. One opening report, then any number of lines, then one closing report.

ProgressBegin.description: Opens a report, saying what has started in the terms the operation itself uses.

kind.description: Marks this payload as the opening of a report.

ProgressReport.description: One line of the operation's own account of itself. It carries no fraction: the operations that report here work through a set whose size is not known when the work starts, so a fraction would have to be invented.

kind.description: Marks this payload as one line of an open report.

message.description: One line of the operation's own output, with surrounding whitespace removed.

ProgressEnd.description: Closes a report. It carries nothing beyond the kind, because the outcome travels on the response the caller is already waiting for.

kind.description: Marks this payload as the close of a report.

PublishDiagnosticsParams.description: The findings for one file, pushed by the daemon when a validation produced them for a document other than the one the request named.

file.description: The file the findings are about.

diagnostics.description: The findings, in the order they were produced.

SuccessResponse.description: The answer to a request that succeeded, carrying the identifier of the request it answers. A response carries no method, so which result shape applies is fixed by the request the identifier belongs to rather than by anything in the response itself.

result.description: The answer, in the shape the method that was asked returns.

ErrorResponse.description: The answer to a request that was refused or failed, carrying the identifier of the request it answers.

ErrorObject.description: What went wrong: a code a client may branch on, a message written for a person to read, and — where the condition has one — the artifacts and source position the message refers to.

message.description: What went wrong, in prose. It is the same wording the same condition carries on every other surface that reports it.

ErrorCode.description: The condition the answer reports. The negative codes are the protocol's own reserved set; the four-digit codes are conditions this daemon raises, each naming a state a client can act on. The set is closed.

oneOf.description: The message could not be parsed as JSON.
The message parsed but is not a well-formed request.
No method of that name exists.
The params the request carried are not admissible: a field the method does not accept, a field of the wrong type, or a value the method refuses.
The daemon failed while doing the work.
The daemon holds no reading of the file and is producing none. The client seeds one by asking for a validation, then retries.
The lockfile for the Release the request named is absent, and the operation needs one.
The entity the request named could not be resolved from the catalog or from the Release the request named.
The daemon is shutting down and is refusing new work. The client does not retry against the same daemon.
A validation of the file is running now and did not finish within the budget the waiting request allowed. The client waits and asks again, sending nothing in the meantime.

ErrorData.description: The artifacts and source position the message refers to, carried structurally so a client need not read them back out of the prose. Every field is optional and a condition populates only what it has in hand; no field stands in for another, so a client learns what it received from the field it read rather than from the code beside it.

file.description: The source document the position fields locate — the document being checked, or the Release whose load failed.

line.description: The line the condition refers to, counted from one.

column.description: The column the condition refers to, counted from one.

end_line.description: The line one past the end of the token the condition refers to. Absent where the token has no recoverable end, in which case a client renders the position as a point.

end_column.description: The column one past the end of the token the condition refers to.

release.description: The Release the condition refers to, spelled the way the request named it, so a client can compose the remedy without reassembling it.

lockfile.description: The lockfile a lockfile-scoped condition is about: the path that was looked for and not found, or could not be read.

unreachable.description: Whether the refusal is a registry the request named that could not be reached: its name did not resolve, a connection to it was refused or could not be opened, or a secure connection to it could not be established. It is read from the failure itself rather than from the message, and it is set only where the failure shows the registry was never reached. A refused index refresh naming one registry carries it; a registry that answered, whatever it answered, leaves it absent.

code.description: The descriptive name of the condition the refusal names, stable across releases: the same value a diagnostic reporting that condition carries in its own code. It is what a client branches on, rather than on the message or on the numeric code beside it, which names the state of the request and stays what it is for every condition. Present exactly when the refusal names a registered condition, and absent when it names none.

shortCode.description: The condition's short code, the letter E and four digits: the form a reader quotes and looks up, and the one that opens the message of a refusal naming a condition. Present exactly when code is.

Diagnostic.description: One finding about one document: where it is, how serious it is, what it says, and the quotable code that names the condition it reports.

line.description: The line the finding is about, counted from one.

column.description: The column the finding is about, counted from one.

oneOf.description: The finding is a fault. A plugin finding of halt severity is reported at this tier.
The finding is reported and is not a fault. A plugin finding of warn severity is reported at this tier.
The finding is information, as a plugin finding of info severity is.

message.description: What the finding says, in prose.

code.description: The condition's descriptive name, stable across releases and quotable in a suppression.

shortCode.description: The condition's short code, the form that opens a halting diagnostic.

classification.description: How the finding was reached, where the condition distinguishes that.

suggest.description: The spelling the finding proposes, where the condition can name one — a near-miss on an identifier, for instance.

keyPath.description: The path through the document to the key the finding is about.

end_line.description: The line one past the end of the token the finding is about, so a client can render the whole token rather than a single character. Absent for a token spanning several lines.

end_column.description: The column one past the end of the token the finding is about.

CodeDescription.description: Where the condition the finding names is explained.

href.description: The published address at which the condition is explained.

Position.description: A place in a document: a line and a character offset within it, both counted from zero. The offset is measured in the units of the encoding the session settled on when it was opened, which is UTF-16 unless the client asked for another.

character.description: The offset within the line, counted from zero, in the units of the encoding the session settled on.

Range.description: A span between two places in a document.

Location.description: A span in a named document.

uri.description: The document the span is in, addressed as a URI.

WorkspaceAndProgressParams.description: The params object of a method that declares no fields of its own. It still admits the two fields every request admits: the workspace it acts on, and a progress token.

InitializeParams.description: Opens a session over a workspace and states what the client can handle. This is the one method on which `workspaceRoot` is a declaration rather than a subject: absent, empty and a path are three different things, and a session opened with no path is one the client has not yet pointed at a workspace.

workspaceRoot.description: The absolute path of the workspace to open. Absent leaves the session with no workspace; an empty string is a path the client supplied and is not the same as sending none.

ClientCapabilities.description: What the client can handle. Unstated is taken as unsupported. Unknown members are ignored rather than refused, so a client may state a capability this daemon does not yet read.

general.description: Capabilities that are not tied to one kind of answer.

positionEncodings.description: The position encodings the client can read, best first.

window.description: Capabilities about what the client can show while work is under way.

workDoneProgress.description: Whether the client can receive progress notifications. A request that mints a progress token in a session which did not declare this is refused.

ValidateParams.description: Checks the workspace, or one document in it, and answers with the findings.

file.description: The document to check. Absent checks what the workspace holds.

content.description: The document's text as the client currently holds it, for checking a buffer that has not been saved. Absent reads the bytes on disk.

release.description: The Release to check against, as a path relative to the workspace root.

InvalidateParams.description: Tells the daemon that a document it holds a reading of has changed, so the next answer about it is computed from the new bytes.

file.description: The document that changed.

granularity.description: How much of what the daemon holds to drop: `file` drops what it holds for the named document only; `workspace`, the default and what any other value is read as, also drops what it holds for the whole workspace.

DiagnosticsParams.description: Answers with the findings the daemon already holds for a document, without checking it again.

file.description: The document to report on. The daemon must already hold a reading of it.

IrGraphParams.description: Answers with the resolved graph a Release compiles to, without rendering it.

release.description: The Release to resolve, as a path relative to the workspace root. An absolute path is refused.

unredacted.description: Whether to answer with the values an author declared sensitive in the clear. Absent or false, each of them is withheld from the graph and a marker naming why stands in its place, as the command line's graph output withholds them; true answers with the graph as the Release compiles to it, those values included.

BuildParams.description: Compiles a Release and writes the rendered artifacts into the workspace.

release.description: The Release to build, as a path relative to the workspace root. An absolute path is refused.

outputParent.description: The directory the output directory is created inside, as a path relative to the workspace root. The artifacts land in the output directory beneath it, laid out as they are beneath the workspace root when nothing is named — so this names the output directory's parent and never the output directory itself. Absent, or empty, writes the output directory beneath the workspace root, as `aggrega build` does wherever it is run from. An absolute path, or one that climbs out of the workspace, is refused.

autoPull.description: Whether to resolve the Release's dependencies first. Asking for it reaches the configured registries and writes the lockfile; unasked, the build reaches no registry.

policyInput.description: The directory to write, beside the artifacts, the payload each governance role hands a plugin attached there, as a path relative to the workspace root — the files `aggrega build --policy-input` writes, by the same names, written whether the build finishes or stops. The answer's notices say how many were written and name each role written no file for. On a request that fails, the files written are on disk and that account is not in the reply: the error carries the refusal alone. Absent writes none. An absolute path, or one that climbs out of the workspace, is refused.

BuildPreviewParams.description: Compiles a Release and reports what writing the artifacts would have produced, writing none of them. It declines the dependency-resolution field the writing build takes, because a request that writes nothing cannot fill a lockfile.

release.description: The Release to compile, as a path relative to the workspace root.

autoPull.description: Accepted on the wire and refused by the method: this request writes nothing, so it cannot fill a lockfile and remain what it says it is.

policyInput.description: The directory to write the payload each governance role hands a plugin attached there into, as a path relative to the workspace root — the files `aggrega build --dry-run --policy-input` writes, by the same names. Sent, they are the one thing this request writes; the output directory and the lockfile are left untouched. The answer's notices say how many were written and name each role written no file for. On a request that fails, the files written are on disk and that account is not in the reply: the error carries the refusal alone. An absolute path, or one that climbs out of the workspace, is refused.

EntityDefinitionParams.description: Answers with what one entity name resolves to and where the document defining it lives.

name.description: The entity to resolve, by name — or a registry reference, `oci://<host>/<repository>:<tag>` or `@<digest>` in place of `:<tag>`, to read the entity published at that coordinate.

release.description: The Release to resolve the name in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. The name is then resolved through the catalog directories the workspace configuration gives that Release, so a name several variants in one workspace declare, one per Release, resolves to the variant that Release builds with, and a name it does not resolve is refused with an account naming that Release's entry under `workspace.releases`. Absent, the name is resolved over the workspace's own catalog directories. A registry reference takes no Release and is refused with one, as is a value that names no Release file.

CatalogIndexParams.description: Answers with the entities the workspace holds: every entity its documents declare, and the Features its catalog directories declare.

release.description: The Release to list the entities in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. The Features are then the ones the catalog directories the workspace configuration gives that Release declare, and a document under a catalog directory only other Releases read is left out, so a workspace keeping variants of one entity side by side, one per Release, is listed with the variant that Release builds with. Absent, the listing is the workspace's own. A value that names no Release file is refused.

ReleaseClosureParams.description: Answers with everything a Release depends on, as resolution reached it.

release.description: The Release to inspect, as a path relative to the workspace root.

ResolveDependenciesParams.description: Resolves a Release's dependencies, pinning them in the lockfile and acquiring the external inputs its render consumes. It reaches the configured registries and it writes.

release.description: The Release to resolve, as a path relative to the workspace root.

upgrade.description: Whether to re-resolve within the declared ranges rather than honouring what the lockfile already pins.

targets.description: The references to re-resolve, leaving the rest pinned as they are. Empty resolves everything.

verify.description: Whether to compare the recorded lockfile against the resolution this request would perform without it, honouring the pins that request would honour, instead of writing it. A verify writes no lockfile, plugin trust record or `entity.lock`; the content cache is read and filled as that resolution would read and fill it. Drift, and a missing lockfile, fail the request. It cannot be combined with `upgrade`, `targets` or `pinSources`, whichever value `pinSources` carries: a request sending one of them beside it is refused as invalid params before anything is resolved.

pinSources.description: Whether to run the pin step `aggrega/pin` runs over the Recipes and FeatureRecipes the Release builds from the workspace's catalog directories, writing the `entity.lock` beside each, rather than refusing the request over one whose lock does not record a pin an input needs. Absent follows the workspace's `pin_sources_at_pull`; either value overrides that setting for this request.

PinParams.description: Records, in the `entity.lock` beside a Recipe or FeatureRecipe, the content pin for every input the entity reads from outside its own document. No Release is named: an input whose identity the entity writes out in full names one artifact for every Release that uses the entity, so nothing a Release supplies is needed to pin it. It reaches the hosts the entity's sources name and it writes beside the entity; the entity document itself is never written.

entity.description: The entity document to pin, as a path relative to the workspace root.

dryRun.description: Whether to answer with the lock the step would write rather than writing it. The inputs are still resolved, so the content cache still fills.

CacheEvictParams.description: Reclaims cached content until what remains fits under a size the request names.

maxSize.description: The size to reclaim down to, written the way a person writes one — for instance 500MB.

SearchParams.description: Searches what the configured registries' local indexes offer. It reads the index already on disk and contacts no registry.

query.description: The text to match against a record's name and description.

kinds.description: The entity kinds to keep. Empty keeps every kind.

selector.description: A label selector the kept records must satisfy.

capabilities.description: The capabilities a kept plugin record must declare.

registry.description: The one registry host to search. Absent searches every configured host.

limit.description: The most records to answer with.

includeRetracted.description: Whether to keep versions a published marker has deprecated.

RegistryAddParams.description: Registers a registry and the trust policy resolution applies to what it serves. It writes the machine-wide configuration file unless the request asks otherwise, so every workspace on the machine resolves through the entry.

name.description: A friendly alias that resolves to the host.

identities.description: The signing identities trusted for what this registry serves.

keyPath.description: The path of a public key to trust, for a registry signed with one rather than with a keyless identity.

trustedRoot.description: The path of the trust anchor to verify signatures against.

requireSignatures.description: Whether an artifact from this registry must carry a verified signature. Absent states nothing and leaves the resolved default in place.

advisory.description: Whether a failed verification is reported rather than halting.

fetchTrust.description: Whether to read the trust policy the registry advertises and pin it. Absent states nothing and leaves the resolved default in place.

global.description: Write the machine-wide configuration file, which is this method's own default.

workspace.description: Write this workspace's own configuration file instead of the machine-wide one.

RegistryRemoveParams.description: Removes a registered registry. It writes the machine-wide configuration file unless the request asks otherwise.

registry.description: The registry to remove, by host or by alias.

global.description: Write the machine-wide configuration file, which is this method's own default.

workspace.description: Write this workspace's own configuration file instead of the machine-wide one.

RegistryUpdateParams.description: Refreshes the local index a search reads, reaching the registry to do it. What it writes is the index under this workspace's own configured cache directory. A registry needing a credential no ambient source carries is refused with the credential named, rather than prompted for.

registry.description: The one registry to refresh. Absent refreshes every configured host.

upgrade.description: Whether to rebuild the index rather than adding to what it already holds.

LogoutParams.description: Removes a stored registry credential. The store is shared by every project on the machine, and the answer says so.

registry.description: The registry whose stored credential to remove.

PublishEntityParams.description: Publishes an entity to a registry. What it lands is what every consumer of that registry resolves, and a published version cannot be recalled from anyone who already fetched it. Nothing is prompted for: identity resolves from what the request supplied or what the environment already carries.

entity.description: The entity document to publish, as a path relative to the workspace root.

registry.description: The registry to publish to. Absent uses the configured default.

dryRun.description: Whether to report what publishing would land without landing it.

sign.description: Whether to sign what is published. Absent states nothing and leaves the resolved default in place.

plugin.description: The plugin module to publish alongside a Plugin entity.

fulcioUrl.description: The certificate authority to obtain a signing certificate from.

rekorUrl.description: The transparency log to record the signature in.

timestampUrl.description: The timestamp authority to countersign with.

identityToken.description: The identity token to sign with, supplied by the caller rather than obtained at a terminal.

pinSources.description: Whether to run the pin step `aggrega/pin` runs on the entity before it is bundled, so the `entity.lock` the step writes beside it is part of what is published. The step runs ahead of every refusal that judges the entity, and under `dryRun` it reports the lock it would write and writes nothing. Absent follows the workspace's `pin_sources_at_push`; either value overrides that setting for this request.

PublishArtifactParams.description: Publishes an arbitrary file to a registry under a name and tag the request gives it.

file.description: The file to publish, as a path relative to the workspace root.

name.description: The repository name to publish under.

mediaType.description: The media type to record for the published bytes.

registry.description: The registry to publish to. Absent uses the configured default.

dryRun.description: Whether to report what publishing would land without landing it.

SignArtifactsParams.description: Signs what is already published. A signature cannot be recalled from anyone who already fetched it.

fulcioUrl.description: The certificate authority to obtain a signing certificate from.

rekorUrl.description: The transparency log to record the signature in.

timestampUrl.description: The timestamp authority to countersign with.

identityToken.description: The identity token to sign with, supplied by the caller rather than obtained at a terminal.

jobs.description: How many references are signed at once. Absent signs one after another. Each reference is still signed exactly as it would be alone — when keyless, with its own certificate and its own transparency-log entry — and the answer keeps the order the references were given.

DeprecateArtifactParams.description: Marks a published version as deprecated, so resolution can report or decline it. The marker is itself published and signed. A request sends either one reference with its content, or a batch file whose entries carry their own — never both, and never content beside the batch file.

reference.description: The published reference to mark. An alternative to `from`: a request carrying both is refused.

severity.description: How strongly the marker speaks — whether resolution reports the version or declines it. Required with `reference`; refused beside `from`, whose batch file carries each marker's own.

oneOf.description: Deprecated, at the milder of the two advisory tiers: still selected when a version is chosen.
Deprecated, at the stronger of the two advisory tiers: still selected when a version is chosen.
Withdrawn: excluded when a version is chosen.

reason.description: Why the version is deprecated. Required with `reference`; refused beside `from`, whose batch file carries each marker's own.

replacement.description: The reference to use instead. Refused beside `from`, whose batch file carries each marker's own.

message.description: What a consumer meeting the marker is told. Refused beside `from`, whose batch file carries each marker's own.

from.description: A batch file of withdrawal entries, as a path relative to the workspace root, attaching one marker per entry. Each entry carries its own reference, severity and reason, and optionally a replacement and a message. An alternative to `reference`: a request carrying both, or carrying a severity, reason, replacement or message beside it, is refused.

fulcioUrl.description: The certificate authority to obtain a signing certificate from.

rekorUrl.description: The transparency log to record the signature in.

timestampUrl.description: The timestamp authority to countersign with.

identityToken.description: The identity token to sign with, supplied by the caller rather than obtained at a terminal.

ResolveParams.description: Answers where the thing under the cursor is defined.

uri.description: The document the cursor is in.

release.description: The Release to answer in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. The definition is then the document the reference resolves to through the catalog directories the workspace configuration gives that Release, in that order, so a name several variants in one workspace declare, one per Release, goes to that Release's variant; where those directories declare no such entity, the workspace's documents are searched, leaving out any under one of the workspace's catalog directories the Release does not read. Absent, the workspace's documents are searched first and the workspace's own catalog directories only where no document declares the name. A value that names no Release file is refused.

FindReferencesParams.description: Answers where the thing under the cursor is referred to.

uri.description: The document the cursor is in.

release.description: The Release to answer in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. A reference made in a document under one of the workspace's catalog directories that the Release does not read is then not reported, so variants a workspace keeps side by side, one per Release, are never reported as one another's references. Absent, every workspace document is searched. A value that names no Release file is refused.

FindImplementationsParams.description: Answers which documents implement the thing under the cursor.

uri.description: The document the cursor is in.

release.description: The Release to answer in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. A document under one of the workspace's catalog directories that the Release does not read is then not reported, so a variant another Release builds with is never listed among this Release's. Absent, every workspace document is searched. A value that names no Release file is refused.

HoverParams.description: Answers with what to show about the thing under the cursor.

uri.description: The document the cursor is in.

release.description: The Release to answer in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. The entity shown is then the one the reference resolves to through the catalog directories the workspace configuration gives that Release, in that order; where those directories declare no such entity, the workspace's documents are searched, leaving out any under one of the workspace's catalog directories the Release does not read. Absent, the workspace's documents are searched first and the workspace's own catalog directories only where no document declares the name. A value that names no Release file is refused.

CompletionParams.description: Answers with what may be written at the cursor.

uri.description: The document the cursor is in.

release.description: The Release to answer in the terms of, as a path relative to the workspace root. The names offered are then those the workspace's documents declare, less the documents under one of the workspace's catalog directories that the Release does not read, together with the Components and Features the catalog directories the workspace configuration gives that Release declare. Absent, they are the workspace's documents and the Components and Features its own catalog directories declare. A value that names no Release file is refused.

CompletionContext.description: What caused the request, where the client tracks it.

triggerCharacter.description: The character that caused it, where a character did.

AttachCandidatesParams.description: Answers which Features may be attached to an entity, judged against that entity's labels, and, for one connection a graph node's component draws, which may fill each slot the connection's socket declares.

node.description: The entity to judge candidates against, by name, read from what the workspace documents declare.

graphNode.description: The graph node to judge candidates against, whose labels are the finalised set the build itself evaluates applicability with. An answer computed over this says what the build will do.

release.description: The Release whose graph the node belongs to, as a path relative to the workspace root. The candidates are then drawn in that Release's terms: the Features the catalog directories the workspace configuration gives that Release declare, and the workspace's documents less any under one of the workspace's catalog directories the Release does not read, so a Feature kept for another Release is never offered for a node of this one's graph.

labels.description: Labels to judge against directly, in place of reading them from an entity or a graph node.

connection.description: One connection drawn by the component of the node graphNode names, to answer for as well as for that node: the answer then also carries slots, each slot the connection's socket declares with the Features that may fill it, or noSlotReason where no slot may be filled. It is sent only with graphNode and release, because a connection exists only on a compiled graph; sent with node or labels it is refused. The candidates beside it keep their meaning, the Features that may attach to the node itself. Its document is accepted and does not change this answer: the slots are the socket's and the candidates the Features', the same whichever document an attachment is written in.

ConnectionCandidatesParams.description: Answers which entities a socket on an entity may be wired to.

node.description: The entity whose sockets are being asked about.

socket.description: The one socket to answer for. Absent answers for every socket the entity declares.

InsertionPointParams.description: Answers where in a document a new entry under a named container belongs, leaving composing and applying the entry to the caller that owns the buffer.

file.description: The document to answer about.

container.description: The path through the document to the container the entry belongs under.

AttachmentContainerParams.description: Answers which document, and where in it, an attachment on a graph node, or on one connection its component draws, belongs.

graphNode.description: The graph node the attachment is for.

release.description: The Release whose graph the node belongs to, as a path relative to the workspace root.

connection.description: One connection the graph node's component draws, when the attachment is for that connection rather than for the node: the answer then names the connection's own features container in the document its document field names, a field required here. In the Aggregate, that is the connection's entry in the document the node was authored in, refused for a connection the Release drew, which the Aggregate holds no entry for. In the Release, it is the per-edge entry under the Release's own entry for the node, whether or not the Release writes one for that connection yet, refused where the Release writes no entry for the node. A connection a Feature drew is refused in either document, because an attachment is written only on a connection a component or the Release draws.

ConnectionAtPositionParams.description: Answers which connection's entry a position in an Aggregate or a Release falls inside: the graph node and the connection, in the terms the candidacy and container requests take them, or why no connection is written there. The entries are the ones an attachment is written in — the entry a component draws a connection with, under the connection's alias, in the document the component was authored in, and every per-edge entry the Release writes — each where the compiled graph records it, so whether a key is a connection is never read from what it is called.

file.description: The document the position is in: the Release, or a document the Release's graph records components as authored in — its Aggregate, or the document of a module that Aggregate imports. It is read from what the session holds for it first, and from disk otherwise.

release.description: The Release whose compiled graph records the connections, as a path relative to the workspace root. It is required for a position in the Aggregate too, because a graph node and a connection exist only on a compiled graph.

ConnectionCoordinate.description: One connection a graph node's component draws, addressed by the socket it is wired through and the alias it carries in that socket, and the document an attachment on it is written in. A connection carries attachments filling the slots its socket declares, and either the Aggregate or the Release may write them.

socket.description: The dependency socket the connection is wired through.

alias.description: The name the connection carries within its socket.

document.description: The document an attachment on the connection is written in. The set is closed, and a value outside it is refused.

oneOf.description: The Aggregate, where the developer writes an attachment on the connection's entry.
The Release, where the operator writes an attachment on the per-edge entry for the connection.

SetActiveReleaseParams.description: Records a Release as the workspace's default by writing a marker in the `.aggrega` directory: the choice `aggrega/activeRelease` reports reads that marker after the configuration's authoring Release. The marker is written inside the workspace and nowhere else: where the `.aggrega` directory or the marker is a link leading out of the workspace, whether or not the place it leads to exists yet, the write is refused naming the link and nothing is written. The answer is the one `aggrega/activeRelease` gives once the marker is written, so it names a different Release where the configuration's authoring Release outranks the marker.

release.description: The Release to record, as a path relative to the workspace root. An absolute path, and one climbing out of the workspace, are refused; so is one leading out of it through a link, unless the workspace configuration names that Release.

EditDocumentParams.description: Applies one bounded edit to a document the workspace carries: one entry added under one container, or one scalar set. The composed document is checked against its kind's schema and reaches disk only if that passes, so this cannot write what the authoring schema refuses. A refused edit leaves the file byte-for-byte as it was.

file.description: The document to edit.

oneOf.description: Adds a component instance under a components container: name is the instance name, value the Component it requests.
Attaches a Feature to the node the request names: name is the attachment's instance name, value the Feature it requests.
Wires a dependency connection from the node the request names, inside socket: name is the alias the connection is addressed by, value the node it points at.
Sets one value on the node the request names: name is the value's key, value a scalar.

node.description: The path through the document to the entry being edited.

socket.description: The socket the edit is about, for an edit that wires one.

value.description: The value the edit writes, in whatever shape the edit takes.

dryRun.description: Whether to answer with the composed document rather than writing it.

ConfigInitParams.description: Seeds a configuration document. It writes the machine-wide file by default, since a registry and the identities trusted on it are machine-wide tooling. It reaches the named registry to read the trust policy it advertises; a registry advertising nothing is reported as such and the seeding proceeds, on the built-in baseline for the official hub and on no policy for any other registry.

registry.description: The registry to seed the configuration for.

force.description: Whether to overwrite a configuration document that already exists.

global.description: Write the machine-wide configuration file, which is this method's own default.

workspace.description: Write this workspace's own configuration file instead of the machine-wide one.

dryRun.description: Whether to answer with the document's content rather than writing it, for a client that keeps its own document model.

ConfigCaptureParams.description: Freezes the resolved configuration into this workspace's own document, so the workspace is self-contained. It always writes that workspace's file and reaches nothing outside it.

allPlugins.description: Whether to freeze every attached plugin rather than only the ones the workspace itself configured.

ImportParams.description: Converts a foreign source description into draft authoring documents, and writes beside them `.aggrega-import.json`, the record of what the import wrote — the target it was given, where it was given one, the catalog snapshot it read, where it read one, each drafted file, and each key of a drafted Aggregate or Release at every depth — which a later sync reads. A source it could not fully convert is an answer rather than a failure: the drafts it did produce are written and the findings say what it could not convert — except under sync, which writes nothing from a conversion that stopped.

source.description: The file or the directory to convert, as an absolute path or one relative to the workspace root; a request without one is refused. It is read where it is, inside the workspace or not, and a directory is read into the files of it the importer's declared file patterns select.

outputDir.description: The directory under the workspace to write the drafts into, relative to the workspace root; an absolute value, or one leading out of the workspace as written or through a link, is refused. Absent writes beneath the workspace root, where the same conversion run at a terminal naming no destination writes. Every drafted path is relative to the directory the answer names as outputDir, under dryRun as well.

format.description: The source format. Absent lets the conversion determine it.

target.description: A provider capability, such as compose or helm — the word a Recipe's spec.capability binds to — to draft a Manifest for beside the drafts, as manifest.yaml: each component type and feature type the drafts need, the types of a catalog Aggregate the drafted one composes included, is mapped to the Recipe or feature recipe of that capability the workspace's catalog offers for it — the one there is, or among several the one named after the type — a type with none, or with several and none so named, is left unmapped with a warning finding naming it, a mapping an importer drafted itself is kept where the catalog offers it for that type and capability and dropped with a warning finding otherwise, and the drafted Release's spec.manifest is set to the Manifest. A capability no Recipe in the catalog binds to is refused before the conversion runs, and nothing is written. Absent drafts no Manifest, except under sync, which drafts for the target the record of the earlier import names; a sync naming a target drafts for it, and the record then names it.

dryRun.description: Whether to answer with the content of every file the request would write rather than writing it. Every other behaviour is the write's, so a request the write would refuse is refused under it too; with sync, it answers with what the sync would write and every part that would drift.

sync.description: Whether to bring what an earlier import drafted beneath outputDir up to date with the source, rather than writing the draft whole. Only what the import wrote changes, as the record beside the drafts lists it: a part the source left alone stays as it is on disk, edited or not; a part the source changed, dropped or gained is written anew, removed — a drafted file deleted whole — or added, where what is on disk is what the import last wrote; and everything else, a key an author added — the environment a drafted Release leaves for its author among them — or a comment not written directly above a drafted key, stays byte for byte. A sync that would change or remove what an author edited or added, or add a part where an author already wrote one, is refused naming each part, and so is a sync over an Aggregate no record lists; nothing is written either way. Without it, a request whose drafts would be written over an Aggregate already in outputDir is refused, under dryRun too.

upgrade.description: Whether to fetch the newest catalog snapshot the workspace's default registry publishes and import against it, holding it from then on in place of the one the workspace holds or the one the record beside the drafts names; it changes nothing where the workspace names a catalog folder, and is refused offline.

answers.description: The answers file the values the drafts leave empty that no source can hold are read from and written to, relative to the workspace root; an absolute value, or one leading out of the workspace as written or through a link, is refused. It holds, under each drafted file's path, the key path inside that document and its answer, and the answers are written into the drafts. Absent reads the one the record beside the drafts names, or else import-answers.yaml beside the source file or inside the source directory. A secret's answer names where the secret comes from — a variable name, ${NAME}, or the name of a Kubernetes Secret — and anything else is refused with nothing written. Nothing is asked: each value still owed is an entry of the answer's owed and a warning finding naming the drafted file, the key and what it is, its answer is sent as answered, and where the drafts are written the last finding says how many are owed and where. Where the drafts include a Release, owe nothing and the conversion finished, its dependencies are then pulled, writing its lockfile, and a pull that fails closes the findings saying why, the drafts written; offline nothing is pulled and a finding names the pull to run. An answer for a key these drafts do not leave empty is kept in the file and not applied, so one answers file serves every target.

answered.description: Answers for values the answer's owed listed, each naming the drafted file and the keys as owed named them. Each is judged, kept in the answers file and written into the drafts exactly as an answer typed at a terminal is: a secret's answer names where the secret comes from — a variable name, ${NAME}, or the name of a Kubernetes Secret — and one that does not is neither kept nor written, its value staying owed with the reason as its secretAdvice. A value the answers file already answers is answered from the file; an empty answer, or one naming a value the drafts do not owe, is not applied. Send it with sync once the drafts are written, since a request that is not a sync is refused over an Aggregate already in outputDir. Under dryRun, which keeps no answer, and under a sync whose conversion stopped, which writes nothing, no answer sent is applied.

ScaffoldEntityParams.description: Drafts a starter document for an entity kind, or writes one of the documentation's runnable examples into a new directory of the workspace, or lists them. Drafting derives the skeleton from the schema set the binary carries, so nothing is read from a workspace and nothing is written — the answer is text, and where it goes is the client's. Writing an example writes the new directory and nothing else, and the examples are read from the signed documentation bundle published for the binary's version, or the newest published before it where none is, verified against the workspace's signature policy before it is kept or read: a bundle that does not verify is refused, and offline only a copy already cached is read. A request sending the fields of two forms together — kind with example or list, list with example, name with example or list, dir without example — is refused before anything is read.

workspaceRoot.description: The absolute path of the workspace. Drafting does not read it. Writing or listing an example requires it: the workspace's configuration decides where the documentation is fetched from and which signatures it must carry, and an example is written inside it.

kind.description: The entity kind to draft, named by its lowercase token, such as component, aggregate, release, recipe or featurerecipe — the token `aggrega/getSchema` lists for it.

name.description: The name to write into the drafted document. Sent only with kind.

example.description: The runnable example to write, by the name the list of examples gives it. Sent instead of kind.

list.description: Whether to answer with every runnable example the documentation publishes, writing nothing. Sent without example and without kind.

dir.description: The new directory to write the example into, relative to the workspace root; absent writes it into a directory named after the example there. It must not exist yet or must be empty: one holding anything is refused and left as it is, and an absolute value, or one leading out of the workspace as written or through a link, is refused before anything is read. Sent only with example.

LintParams.description: Checks catalog publishing conventions over one entity, over everything a Release's closure reaches, or over everything under the configured catalog directories. Nothing is written under any mode. Naming neither an entity nor a Release checks the whole catalog: in a workspace whose configuration gives no Release catalog directories of its own, once over the workspace's directories; in a workspace that names Releases under workspace.releases, once for each Release over the directories that Release reads, never over all of them together.

entity.description: The one entity document to check.

release.description: The Release whose closure to check, as a path relative to the workspace root.

prePublish.description: Whether to compare each entity against its previously published version, which reaches the configured registries.

PluginAddParams.description: Attaches a plugin to a socket the workspace configures. It reaches a registry to resolve the query to one plugin and to pin a version. The one decision a terminal would obtain — accepting a command-extension plugin's declared capabilities — arrives as a field here, so the client asks whoever is driving it and this surface never waits on a prompt.

type.description: The socket the plugin attaches to.

query.description: What to resolve to one plugin.

capability.description: The capability the attachment is for, where the socket carries several.

role.description: The role the attachment runs in, which fixes what it may emit.

workspace.description: Write this workspace's own configuration file.

acceptCapabilities.description: Whether the caller accepts the capabilities a command-extension plugin declares.

dryRun.description: Whether to answer with the configuration document's content rather than writing it.

PluginRemoveParams.description: Detaches a plugin from a socket the workspace configures.

type.description: The socket the plugin is attached to.

workspace.description: Write this workspace's own configuration file.

PluginSyncParams.description: Aligns a Plugin entity's machine-owned records with the module it points at. It rewrites those records and carries every other byte of the document through unchanged.

entity.description: The Plugin entity document to align.

plugin.description: The plugin module to read the records from.

PluginGenCatalogParams.description: Generates Plugin catalog documents from a plugin's own declared metadata plus an authored overlay. Regenerating over unchanged inputs produces byte-identical documents.

fromEmbedded.description: Whether to read the metadata from the plugins the binary already carries.

plugin.description: The plugin module to read the metadata from.

outputDir.description: The directory under the workspace to write the documents into.

overlay.description: The authored document whose content is merged over the generated metadata.

dryRun.description: Whether to answer with the documents' content rather than writing them.

ExplainErrorParams.description: Expands a code a finding carried into what the compiler declares about that condition and the published entries that teach the authoring fix. It acquires the published documentation when the workspace has no copy; one it cannot acquire still answers what the binary declares, and says why the prose is missing.

code.description: The condition to expand, named by either the code a finding carried or its short code.

GetSchemaParams.description: Answers with a kind's schema, or — when no kind is named — with which kinds can be named. It answers for the running binary rather than for whichever copy is installed elsewhere, so it needs no workspace and reads none.

kind.description: The kind whose schema to answer with. Absent answers with the kinds that can be named instead.

SkillsInstallParams.description: Writes the assistant skill built into the binary into the skill folder of each assistant the request names or, for a global request naming none, each assistant found on this machine. Without global it writes each assistant's project folder inside the workspace the request names, and every path it would write there is held to that workspace; with global it writes each assistant's per-user folder under the home directory. Every target is checked before anything is written, so a refusal leaves every folder as it was.

agents.description: The assistants to install the skill for, by the identifiers the listing reports. A project request naming none is refused. A global request naming none installs the skill for the assistants found on this machine, each one whose configuration folder is in the home directory or whose command is on the PATH, and is refused with nothing written where none is found. An identifier no skill folder is known for is refused, by name, and an identifier given twice is installed once.

global.description: Write each assistant's per-user skill folder under the home directory, which it reads in every project, instead of its project folder in the workspace.

ServerCapabilities.description: What the daemon will do in this session, settled against what the client said it can handle.

positionEncoding.description: The encoding every position in this session is expressed in.

workDoneProgress.description: Whether the daemon will send progress notifications in this session. Present only where the client declared it can receive them.

ClosureEntity.description: One entity a Release depends on, at the version resolution settled.

uri.description: The reference the entity resolves from.

version.description: The version that was settled on.

source.description: Where the run that produced this entry took the entity from, in the same word `aggrega pull --detail` prints for it: `fetched-fresh` (fetched from a registry during that run), `cache-reuse` (a copy already in the cache, reused without fetching), `local` (found on the local filesystem, such as a catalog directory), `in-binary` (the copy inside the compiler binary), or `external` (the Release's own Aggregate or Manifest, read from the file or entry the Release names rather than resolved as one of its dependencies; an Aggregate the run fetched from a registry is `fetched-fresh` instead). Present on the entries of a dependency resolution's report, where it describes what that run did on this machine, and absent from a listing of a Release's resolved dependencies, which describes what the Release depends on. The lockfile records no source. Omitted for an entity whose source the run did not record.

ToolchainCorePlugin.description: One plugin the compiler itself carries, and the version of it that was used.

ToolchainReport.description: The compiler that resolved, and the plugins it carries.

corePlugins.description: The plugins the compiler carries, with the version of each that was used.

DependencyResolutionReport.description: What a dependency resolution pinned and acquired.

lockfile.description: The lockfile the resolution wrote, or the one a verify compared against.

verified.description: Whether the request was a verify, which compared the recorded lockfile and wrote no lockfile, plugin trust record or `entity.lock`.

entities.description: The entities the resolution pinned, or a verify compared.

libraries.description: The libraries the resolution pinned, or a verify compared.

plugins.description: The plugins the resolution pinned, or a verify compared.

sourceArtifacts.description: How many source artifacts were acquired.

trustedPlugins.description: How many of the pinned plugins carried a verified signature.

externalInputs.description: How many external inputs the render consumes were acquired.

incompleteExternalInputs.description: Which external inputs could not be acquired, where some could not be.

BuildNotice.description: One thing the build wants the caller to know, which is neither a finding about a document nor a failure.

class.description: What kind of notice this is.

CacheScope.description: How far a cache answer reaches. Two of the cache classes are shared by every project on the machine, so every cache answer names which ones it touched — a session opened over one workspace would otherwise be read as reporting only about that workspace.

machineWideClasses.description: The cache classes this answer touched that are shared across every project on the machine.

sizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

digest.description: The content digest the entry is keyed under, where it has one.

note.description: Anything else worth saying about the entry.

CacheClass.description: One cache the daemon reports on.

reach.description: Whether the cache belongs to this workspace or is shared across the machine.

prunable.description: Whether reclaiming this cache is something the daemon will do.

CacheProvenance.description: Which identities a cached artifact was acquired under, and how widely it is shared.

identities.description: The identities the artifact is attributed to.

sharedBy.description: How many holders share the artifact.

CacheRemoval.description: One thing a reclamation removed — or, in a list of what it left in place, one thing it would have removed.

reach.description: Whether that cache belongs to this workspace or is shared across the machine.

size.description: How many bytes it occupies, or occupied before it was removed.

sizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

CacheShortfall.description: What a reclamation left behind, and what would reclaim it, so a caller reading a smaller figure than it expected learns why rather than inferring it.

class.description: Which cache holds what was left.

sizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

reach.description: Whether that cache belongs to this workspace or is shared across the machine.
Whether it belongs to this workspace or is shared across the machine.

size.description: How many bytes were reclaimed from it.

sizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

heldOpenFiles.description: How many files the clearing left in this cache because another process had them open. Only Windows refuses to remove an open file, so everywhere else this is zero. A later clearing removes them once that process has finished with them.

heldOpenBytes.description: How many bytes those files occupy. They are not counted in size, which is what the clearing reclaimed.

heldOpenBytesText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

ConfigWriteScope.description: Which configuration document was written and how far it reaches. A request names one workspace, so an answer that said nothing would be read as being about that workspace — and for a machine-wide write that reading is wrong.

machineWide.description: Whether that document is the one every workspace on the machine resolves through.

PluginWriteScope.description: Which configuration document a plugin change was written into and how far it reaches. The command-extension socket's own default is the machine-wide document, so every answer says which one it wrote.

machineWide.description: Whether that document is the one every workspace on the machine resolves through.

CredentialStoreScope.description: How far a credential change reaches. The store is shared by every project on the machine and by every other tool addressing the same registries, so the answer reports that rather than leaving a session-scoped reading to be inferred.

machineWide.description: Whether the store the change touched is shared across the machine.

SkillFolderScope.description: How far a skill installation reaches. A request names one workspace, so an answer that said nothing would be read as being about that workspace — and for the per-user folders, which an assistant reads in every project, that reading is wrong.

machineWide.description: Whether the folders written are the per-user ones under the home directory, which the assistant reads in every project on the machine.

PublicationReach.description: How far a publication reached. These answers reach beyond this machine entirely — what they attach is what every consumer of that registry resolves — so each names every registry it addressed and whether the call attached anything there.

registries.description: Every registry host the call addressed, each named once, in the order the call first addressed it. A single-reference call names one; a dry run names the destination it would have addressed.

beyondThisMachine.description: Whether the call attached anything a registry now serves to others: uploaded content, a signature, a publication date or a deprecation marker. False on a dry run, and on a call that found everything it would have attached already there — a publication run again over a complete version, or a signing batch whose every reference already carried a signature that verifies.

WorkspaceEntityRef.description: One entity, by kind and name, with the document that declares it.

file.description: The document declaring it, as a path relative to the workspace root.

SourcedEntityRef.description: One entity, with where it was read from. A workspace document reports its workspace-relative path; an entity resolved from the configured catalog directories reports an empty path, because the only path it has would mean nothing to a client. The origin says which of the two it is, rather than leaving an empty path to be read as a field nobody filled in.

file.description: The document declaring it, as a path relative to the workspace root, or empty where it came from the configured catalog directories.

origin.description: Where the entity was read from.

SocketCandidacy.description: One socket on an entity, and what may be wired into it.

selector.description: The label selector a target must satisfy.

required.description: Whether the socket must be wired for the build to proceed.

targets.description: The entities that may be wired into it.

SlotCandidacy.description: One slot a connection's socket declares, as the consuming Component declares it on the socket, and the Features that may fill it on that connection.

slot.description: The slot's name, which is the key an attachment filling it is written under in the connection's features.

selector.description: The label selector a Feature filling the slot must satisfy with its own labels. Empty where the slot declares none, which admits any Feature.

required.description: Whether every connection wired through the socket must fill the slot for the build to proceed.

inject.description: The delivery mechanisms the slot permits for what fills it, in the order the Component declares them. Empty where it declares none.

sensitive.description: Whether the slot declares that what fills it handles secret material. It marks the attachment filling it and refuses nothing.

description.description: What the Component says the slot is for. Empty where it says nothing.

candidates.description: Each Feature that may fill the slot on this connection: one whose declared applicability the graph node's labels satisfy, which every attachment the node carries is held to, and whose own labels satisfy the slot's selector. A Feature whose applicability or whose labels cannot be read against the selector is not offered, because a build refuses rather than admits it.

CatalogEntity.description: One entity the workspace index holds.

apiVersion.description: The schema version the document declares.

description.description: What the document says the entity is for.

file.description: The document declaring it, as a path relative to the workspace root.

origin.description: Where the entity was read from.

CompletionItem.description: One thing that may be written at the cursor.

kind.description: What sort of thing it is, so a client can choose an icon for it.

detail.description: A short qualifier shown beside the label.

documentation.description: What the thing is, at length.

sortText.description: The value to order by, where it differs from the label.

MarkupContent.description: Text to show, and how it is marked up.

kind.description: How the text is marked up.

EntityKindDescriptor.description: One kind an author writes a document of, pairing the token a request names with the kind the document itself declares, and saying which operations accept a document of that kind.

kind.description: The lowercase token a request names, such as component or featurerecipe.

documentKind.description: The kind the document's own header declares.

acceptedBy.description: Which operations accept a document of this kind named on its own — by its path, or by its name for inspection — with nothing else sent beside it. A member is true when that operation does not refuse a document for being of this kind; a document it accepts may still be refused for what the document says.

EntityKindAcceptance.description: For one kind an author writes, whether each operation accepts a document of that kind named on its own. Every member is present on every entry, so false is a statement rather than an omission.

singleEntityValidation.description: Whether the single-entity scope of `aggrega validate` — the command given one document's path — checks a document of this kind. A kind it refuses is checked by the whole-catalog scope or by the Release scope instead.

publication.description: Whether `aggrega/publishEntity` naming the document alone publishes a document of this kind. A kind whose publication also binds an executable named beside the document — a Plugin — is false, because a request naming the document alone is refused for it; a Manifest and a Release are false because neither kind is published.

inspectionByName.description: Whether `aggrega/entityDefinition` resolves a name to an entity of this kind, the name sent as it is written where one entity references another.

RegistryTrust.description: The trust policy resolution applies to what a registry serves.

signaturesRequired.description: Whether an artifact from this registry must carry a verified signature.

advisory.description: Whether a failed verification is reported rather than halting.

anchor.description: The trust anchor signatures are verified against.

keylessIdentities.description: How many signing identities are trusted for this registry.

Registry.description: One configured registry. No field here carries credential material, its length, its shape, or any rendering of it — presence is the whole of what is reported, which is what makes the value safe to paste into an issue.

host.description: The registry host, which is its identity.

name.description: The friendly alias that resolves to the host, where one is configured.

default.description: Whether this is the registry an operation with no registry named addresses.

authState.description: Whether a credential for this host is present in the machine-wide store. It is reported even when empty, so a caller can tell 'no credential is present' from 'the listing did not look'.

TrustFetchOutcome.description: What reading a registry's advertised trust policy did. The outcomes are kept apart because they mean different things: the advertised policy was taken, the registry advertised nothing — which is not a failure — the built-in baseline was pinned in its place, or no read was attempted. Where nothing was advertised, whether the registry could be reached at all is stated beside it.

pinned.description: Whether the advertised policy was taken.

notAdvertised.description: Whether the registry was asked and advertised no policy, in which case the operation proceeds on what the request stated. A registry the offline posture kept from being asked is never reported this way. A registry that could not be reached is reported this way too, since no policy came back from it, and carries unreachable beside it; read unreachable to tell the two apart.

unreachable.description: Whether the registry could not be reached when its advertised policy was asked for: its name did not resolve, a connection to it was refused or could not be opened, or a secure connection to it could not be established. It is read from the failure itself rather than from reason, it stands beside notAdvertised, and it is set only where the failure shows the registry was never reached; a registry that answered — with no policy, or with a failure — leaves it absent.

baseline.description: Whether the built-in baseline was pinned because no advertised policy was taken, which only the official hub carries. It stands beside notAdvertised where the hub was asked and advertised nothing, and alone where the offline posture kept the hub from being asked.

skipped.description: Whether no read was attempted, because a stated policy overrode it or the request asked for none.

identities.description: How many signing identities the advertised policy carried.

reason.description: Why the advertised policy was not taken: what the registry's endpoint did, or the offline refusal that kept it from being asked.

SkippedRepo.description: One repository the index walk passed over, and why.

repo.description: The repository that was passed over.

DeprecationNote.description: One deprecation marker the index walk met, and what it did with it. A marker that was honoured and one that was present and declined are reported on the same footing, so recording many does not pass in silence while declining one announces itself.

repo.description: The repository the marker is on.

recorded.description: Whether the marker's own signature verified, and the index therefore carries it.

oneOf.description: Deprecated, at the milder of the two advisory tiers: still selected when a version is chosen.
Deprecated, at the stronger of the two advisory tiers: still selected when a version is chosen.
Withdrawn: excluded when a version is chosen.

HostUpdate.description: What an index refresh did for one registry.

host.description: The registry host that was refreshed.

deprecationsExamined.description: Whether the walk looked for deprecation markers at all. It is separate from the count because 'this registry published none' and 'this run had no basis to judge one' are different facts.

skipped.description: The repositories the walk passed over.

readsRetried.description: How many of the walk's reads the registry refused or dropped in passing and were asked again, each read counted once however many attempts it took and whether or not it then succeeded; zero where none was. A walk whose reads all succeeded in the end lists no repository under `skipped`, so this count is what says how close it came to leaving one out.

error.description: What failed for this host, so a walk over several reports which of them failed without the caller correlating anything.

unreachable.description: Whether this registry could not be reached: its name did not resolve, a connection to it was refused or could not be opened, or a secure connection to it could not be established. It is read from the failure itself rather than from error, it is set only beside error, and only where the failure shows the registry was never reached; a registry that answered, whatever it answered, leaves it absent.

PublishedVersion.description: One version the index holds for a reference: the manifest digest its tag resolved to when the index was built; where the trust policy the index was built under verified the version's own signature, the signer it verified as; and, where anything records it, when the version was published, with the source that says so. The signer is absent for a version with no signature, for one none of whose signatures verified, and where that policy pins neither a public key nor a trusted identity or switches signature verification off. None of those is a basis for naming a signer, and its absence says nothing more. The publication date is absent where the publication stated none and no keyless signature that policy verified records one.

version.description: The version, as its tag names it.

manifestDigest.description: The digest of the manifest the version's tag resolved to when the index was built, which addresses the version by the bytes it names rather than by its tag.

publishedAt.description: When the version was published, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC to the second. Where it came from is `publishedAtSource`, and the two are present together or not at all.

publishedAtSource.description: Where `publishedAt` came from, so a time a transparency log attests is never mistaken for one the publisher states. The set is closed.

oneOf.description: The time a transparency log recorded the version's keyless signature, which the trust policy the index was built under verified along with the log's signed promise of that time. For a version signed as it was published, it is the publication; for one signed afterwards, it is when that signature was made.

The time the publication stated beside what it published, from the publishing machine's own clock. Nothing attests it. A publication states one where its signature carries no attested time: a keyed signature, or none. Where several are attached, the earliest is taken.

VerifiedSignature.description: A signature that verified against a registry's trust policy: how it verified, the signer it verified as, and the digest of the signature bundle that verified.

bundleDigest.description: The digest of the signature bundle that verified, as `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters.

identity.description: The signer the signature verified as: for a keyless signature, the identity the signing certificate was issued for, which is its subject alternative name; for a keyed signature, `keyed:sha256:` followed by the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the pinned public key's PEM text.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer recorded in the signing certificate, for a keyless signature. It is absent for a keyed signature.

mode.description: How the signature verified. The set is closed.

oneOf.description: Against a signing certificate whose identity and issuer match one the policy trusts, which chains to the trust root the policy pins or, where it pins none, to the public-good Sigstore root, and whose signature a transparency log records.
Against the public key the policy pins.

RegistrySearchRecord.description: One record a search matched, as the local index holds it, plus which of its versions a published marker has deprecated.

uri.description: The reference the record resolves from.

version.description: The version the record is keyed at.

versions.description: Every version the index holds for this reference.

category.description: The category the entity is published under.

pluginType.description: The socket a plugin record attaches to.

capabilities.description: The capabilities a plugin record declares.

manifestDigest.description: The digest of the published manifest.

listingDigest.description: The digest of the listing the record was read from.

deprecations.description: The deprecation markers the index carries for this reference, each with the version it covers and the verified marker itself.

published.description: Every version the index holds for this reference, in the same order as `versions`, each with the manifest digest its tag resolved to when the index was built, where the trust policy the index was built under verified that version's own signature its verified signer, and where anything records it its publication date and that date's source. A version recorded with no signer carries no signature that policy verified, and nothing more is said about it. Only manifests, signature attachments and publication-date attachments are read from the registry to record this; no entity's content is fetched.

retracted.description: The versions a published marker has deprecated.

host.description: The host whose index was searched.

lastUpdated.description: When the index was last refreshed. It is absent rather than zero when the snapshot carries no time, so a caller can tell 'not recorded' from the epoch.
