EffectiveConfigurationSetting.description: One resolved setting, and which document it came from.

ImportedFile.description: One file an import writes: a draft document, or the record of what the import wrote.

path.description: Where the file belongs, as a path relative to the answer's outputDir.

change.description: How the part drifted: added, for a part the source gained; removed, for one it dropped; or changed, for one it changed.

file.description: The drafted file the part is in, as a path relative to the answer's outputDir.

key.description: The keys leading to the part from the top of a drafted Aggregate or Release, one entry per key, so a key holding a full stop stays one entry. Empty where the part is the whole file.

ImportOwed.description: One value the drafts still leave empty that no source could supply and no answer did.

file.description: The drafted file the value is in, as a path relative to the answer's outputDir.

key.description: The keys leading to the value from the top of that document, one entry per key, so a key holding a full stop stays one entry. An answer sent as answered names the value by these keys.

question.description: What the value is: its schema's description, or else the comment the draft writes above its key, or else what its schema says it takes.

sensitive.description: Whether the value is a secret's, whose answer names where the secret comes from and never holds the secret itself.

secretAdvice.description: Present on a secret's value: what its answer must be, in the sentence a person answering it at a terminal is shown — or, where the answer sent for it as answered was refused, why it was refused.

ImportAnswered.description: One answer for a value the answer's owed listed.

file.description: The drafted file the value is in, as owed names it.

key.description: The keys leading to the value, as owed names them.

answer.description: The answer. An empty one leaves the value owed.

code.description: The condition's quotable name, where it has one.

rationale.description: Why the importer made the choice, in its own words. Absent where it wrote none.

swapHint.description: How to swap the choice for an alternative, in the importer's own words. Absent where it wrote none.

type.description: The node's type, as the source names it.

paramsSummary.description: A summary of the node's parameters, for showing beside the decision.

score.description: How well the Component matches the node, as the importer scored it.

tier.description: The match tier the score falls in.

table.description: The contribution of the mapping-table signal.

category.description: The contribution of the category signal.

domainLabels.description: The contribution of the domain-labels signal.

shape.description: The contribution of the shape signal.

name.description: The contribution of the name signal.

target.description: The name of the Component chosen: an existing catalog Component, or the one drafted for the node.

tier.description: The match tier of the choice.

file.description: The document.

PluginRetractionExclusion.description: One version that was available and not chosen.

default.description: The value used when the flag is not passed.

PluginCLICommand.description: One top-level command verb a plugin contributes.

flags.description: The command's flags, in declared order.

uri.description: The reference the attachment resolves from.

capability.description: The capability the attachment is for.

attachments.description: The attachments that were frozen onto it.

digest.description: The digest of what was signed.

DeprecationMarked.description: One published version a deprecation marked.

oneOf.description: Deprecated, at the milder of the two advisory tiers: still selected when a version is chosen.
Deprecated, at the stronger of the two advisory tiers: still selected when a version is chosen.
Withdrawn: excluded when a version is chosen.

digest.description: The digest of the marker that was published.

workspaceRoot.description: The workspace the session opened over.

ValidateResult.description: What checking found, and how much was checked.

diagnostics.description: The findings. It is null rather than an empty list when there are none.

IrGraphResult.description: The resolved graph a Release compiles to.

graph.description: The graph document. The values an author declared sensitive are withheld from it unless the request asked for them with unredacted; everything else is carried through as the compiler emitted it. Its own shape is the graph's published contract and is not restated here.

outputDirectory.description: The directory the artifacts were written into.

files.description: The artifacts that were written, as paths relative to the output directory.

notices.description: Anything the build wants the caller to know that is neither a finding nor a failure.

BuildPreviewResult.description: What a build would have written. Nothing was written, so there is no output directory to name.

files.description: The artifacts writing would have produced.

notices.description: Anything the compile wants the caller to know that is neither a finding nor a failure.

EntityDefinitionResult.description: What an entity name resolves to, and the document defining it. An answer read from a registry reference carries `published`, and an answer the catalog resolved by name never does.

description.description: What the document says the entity is for.

publishScope.description: How widely the entity is published.

file.description: The document defining it.

authoredLength.description: How many bytes the authored document holds, so a client can tell an authored document from a resolved rendering of one.

PublishedArtifact.description: What a registry reference read: the coordinate, how it held the entity, and the manifest it was read through. Every field is present wherever this is.

archive.description: Whether the coordinate's bytes were an archive the entity document was unpacked from. False where the coordinate held the entity document itself.

mediaType.description: The artifact type the manifest declares.

manifestDigest.description: The digest of the manifest the entity was read through — the value to name after `@` to read the same bytes again exactly.

release.description: The Release that was inspected.

mappingDiagnostics.description: What resolving the Manifest's mappings had to say.

deprecations.description: The deprecation markers the closure met.

lockfile.description: The lockfile the resolution wrote, or the one a verify compared against.

verified.description: Whether the request was a verify, which compared the recorded lockfile and wrote no lockfile, plugin trust record or `entity.lock`.

entities.description: The entities the resolution pinned, or a verify compared.

libraries.description: The libraries the resolution pinned, or a verify compared.

plugins.description: The plugins the resolution pinned, or a verify compared.

sourceArtifacts.description: How many source artifacts were acquired.

trustedPlugins.description: How many of the pinned plugins carried a verified signature.

externalInputs.description: How many external inputs the render consumes were acquired.

incompleteExternalInputs.description: Which external inputs could not be acquired, where some could not be.

notices.description: Anything the resolution wants the caller to know.

PinResult.description: What the pin step did to the lock beside an entity, or would do on a dry run. It is the answer to `aggrega/pin`, and a publication that ran the step carries it as its `pin`.

entity.description: The entity document the step read, as a path relative to the workspace root.

kind.description: The entity's kind, as its document declares it.

name.description: The entity's name, as its document declares it.

pinnable.description: Whether an entity of this kind reads anything a lock records a pin for, which a Recipe and a FeatureRecipe do. Where it is false nothing beside the entity was touched, `changed` is false, and `lock`, `removed`, `pins` and `content` are absent.

lock.description: The lock the step wrote, or would write, as a path relative to the workspace root.

changed.description: Whether the lock moved, or would move on a dry run. False where the lock already recorded every pin the entity needs and was left byte-identical.

removed.description: Whether the move is a removal: the entity reads nothing a lock records a pin for, so no lock is left beside it.

dryRun.description: Whether this reports what the step would do rather than what it did.

pins.description: How many pins of each class the lock holds after the step, or would hold after a dry run. Every class the lock can hold is listed, a class with no pin included.

content.description: The lock a dry run would write. Absent where the lock would be left as it is or removed, and on every answer that is not a dry run.

PinClassCount.description: How many pins of one class a lock holds.

class.description: The class of pin, in the words a refusal naming a missing one uses — `remote source` or `imported file`, for instance.

pins.description: How many pins of that class the lock holds.

CacheStatusResult.description: What the caches serving this workspace hold.

classes.description: Each cache and what it holds.

provenance.description: Which identities the cached artifacts were acquired under.

totalCount.description: How many entries the caches hold in total.

totalSize.description: How many bytes they occupy in total.

totalSizeText.description: The same total written the way a person reads one.

CachePruneResult.description: What a reclamation removed, what it kept, and what it could not reclaim.

heldOpen.description: What the prune would have removed but left in place because another process had it open. Only Windows refuses to remove an open file, so everywhere else this is empty. These entries are counted as neither removed nor kept, none of their bytes count as reclaimed, and a later prune reclaims them; an entry that is a directory may already have lost the files in it that were not open.

reclaimedBytesText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

unattributedCount.description: How many entries no holder claims.

unattributedSizeText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

notPruneEligible.description: What was left behind, and what would reclaim it.

CacheEvictResult.description: What reclaiming down to a size removed, and what remains.

withinCapBefore.description: Whether what was held already fitted under the size, so nothing needed removing.

heldOpen.description: What the reclaiming would have removed but left in place because another process had it open; it went on to the next-oldest entry instead. Only Windows refuses to remove an open file, so everywhere else this is empty. These entries still count toward the bytes that remain, and a later reclaiming can remove them.

totalBefore.description: How many bytes were held before.

totalBeforeText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

reclaimedBytesText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

remainingBytesText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

capBytes.description: The size that was reclaimed down to, in bytes.

capBytesText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

reclaimedBytesText.description: The same figure written the way a person reads one.

RegistryListResult.description: The registries this workspace resolves through.

credentialStateIsMachineWide.description: Whether the credential presence reported for each registry is a machine-wide fact rather than a workspace one. It is reported so a session-scoped answer is not read as denying the wider reach.

SearchResult.description: What the local registry indexes offered for the search.

indexes.description: Each searched host and when its index was last refreshed.

missingIndexHosts.description: The configured hosts with no local index to search, so a short answer is explained rather than left to be inferred.

stale.description: Whether any searched index is old enough to be worth refreshing.

registriesConfigured.description: Whether any registry is configured at all, which distinguishes 'nothing matched' from 'nothing was searched'.

RegistryAddResult.description: What registering a registry wrote, where, and what it read from the registry itself.

host.description: The host the entry is keyed under, which is not always the spelling the request used.

RegistryRemoveResult.description: What removing a registry wrote, and where.

host.description: The host whose entry was removed.

RegistryUpdateResult.description: What refreshing the local indexes did, per host.

hosts.description: What the refresh did for each host.

failed.description: The hosts the refresh could not complete.

indexRoot.description: The directory the indexes were written under.

registriesConfigured.description: Whether any registry is configured at all.

reachedRegistries.description: Always true on this answer: refreshing the indexes goes out to the registries themselves, where listing them and searching answer from configuration and from a local index. Whether a given registry was in fact reached is stated on its own entry in hosts, by unreachable.

LogoutResult.description: Which stored credential was removed, and how far the store reaches.

registry.description: The registry whose credential was removed.

PublishEntityResult.description: What publishing an entity landed, and where. A publication that ran the pin step first also carries what that step did, as `pin`, which is absent where the step did not run.

reference.description: The reference the entity was published under.

tag.description: The tag it was published under.

kind.description: The entity kind that was published.

mediaType.description: The media type recorded for the published bytes.

sizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

pluginSize.description: How many bytes the plugin module published alongside a Plugin entity occupies.

pluginSizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

digest.description: The digest of what was published. On a dry run, the digest a publication of the same content would land, computed from the content alone: the one `aggrega push --dry-run` prints.

signed.description: Whether this publication attached a signature: the one it made before publishing, or, on a version already published, one the version lacked.

alreadyPublished.description: Whether the same bytes were already there, so no content was uploaded. Only what that publication still lacked was attached beside it: its publication date and, where this publication signs, its signature; signed says whether a signature was.

dryRun.description: Whether this reports what publishing would have landed rather than what it did.

wholeDirectorySource.description: The entity's local source as authored, present when it is written as a template. Such a source names its directory only once a Release fills the template in, so the publication carries every file in the entity's directory rather than only the files the entity names. Absent where it carries only those files.

windowsUnusableEntries.description: The entries of the published archive whose path holds a part Windows cannot hold as written — a name Windows reserves for a device, such as CON, AUX or NUL, in any letter case and whatever extension follows, or a part ending in a full stop or a space — the entity document's own file name first, then the files it carries. A workspace on Windows refuses to unpack them, so it cannot use the version; the publication goes ahead or stops exactly as it would without them. Absent where there is none, which includes an entity published as its document alone.

PublishArtifactResult.description: What publishing a file landed, and where.

reference.description: The reference the file was published under.

tag.description: The tag it was published under.

mediaType.description: The media type recorded for the published bytes.

sizeText.description: The same size written the way a person reads one.

digest.description: The digest of what was published.

alreadyPublished.description: Whether the same bytes were already there, so no content was uploaded. A publication date was attached beside it only where the artifact lacked one.

dryRun.description: Whether this reports what publishing would have landed rather than what it did.

SignArtifactsResult.description: What was signed, and where the signatures landed.

DeprecateArtifactResult.description: What was marked deprecated, and where the markers landed.

ResolveResult.description: Where the thing under the cursor is defined.

location.description: Where it is defined. It is null where nothing under the cursor resolves to a definition.

FindReferencesResult.description: Where the thing under the cursor is referred to.

locations.description: Each place it is referred to.

FindImplementationsResult.description: Which documents implement the thing under the cursor.

contents.description: What to show. It is null where there is nothing to say about what is under the cursor.

CompletionResult.description: What may be written at the cursor.

items.description: Each thing that may be written.

CatalogIndexResult.description: Every entity the workspace index holds, and the links leading out of the workspace, to directories and to files, that were not read for it.

unreadLinkedDirs.description: Each link under the workspace root that leads to a directory outside it, named relative to the root where the link itself sits, in the order the workspace is searched. No directory outside the root is searched, so no document behind one of these links is among entities as the workspace's own, and a client listing entities can say why. Not named: a link to a directory inside the root, which is searched, or left out, where it actually sits; a link wherever a directory would be left out, whether by where it sits, by its name or by a .gitignore; a link that cannot be resolved, because it leads nowhere or round a loop; and, in an answer given in a Release's terms, a link under a catalog directory only other Releases read. Empty when the workspace holds none.

unreadLinkedFiles.description: Each link under the workspace root that is named like a YAML file, its own name ending in .yaml or .yml, and leads to a file outside the root, named relative to the root where the link itself sits, in the order the workspace is searched. Such a file is not read for the index, whatever it declares, so the entity it declares is not among entities as the workspace's own, and a client listing entities can say why; the configured catalog directories are how entities outside the workspace are read. Not named: a link to a file that the workspace configuration names as a Release, as build.authoring_release or as a key of workspace.releases, and that declares one, which is read and listed in entities at the link's own place; a link to a file inside the root, which is read at the link's own place; a link a .gitignore leaves out, or one inside a directory the search leaves out; a link that leads to no file, whether to a directory, which unreadLinkedDirs names where it leads out of the root, or nowhere, or round a loop; and, in an answer given in a Release's terms, a link under a catalog directory only other Releases read. A workspace configuration file that is a link leading out of the workspace, its own .aggrega-config.yaml or the CI-owned overlay beside it, is named whether or not the search met it, after the links the search named: the workspace's configuration is then not read at all, this answer is the workspace's own index read with nothing configured, so no catalog directory is read for it, and every request the configuration decides, an index in a Release's terms included, is refused for that workspace with the read hold's condition. Empty when the workspace holds none.

AttachCandidatesResult.description: Which Features may be attached to the entity, and the labels they were judged against; and, for a connection the request named, the slots its socket declares with the Features that may fill each.

node.description: The entity the candidates were judged for.

nodeLabels.description: The labels the judgement was made against.

labelSource.description: Which label set was used, which is not cosmetic: a document's declared labels are what a reading of the source can see, while a graph node's are the finalised set the build itself judges against. An answer computed over the second is a statement about what the build will do.

candidates.description: Each Feature that may be attached.

slots.description: Present only when the request named a connection: each slot the connection's socket declares, in the order the Component declares them, with the Features that may fill it. Empty when no slot may be filled on the connection, and noSlotReason then says why — which a client reads rather than taking an empty list for slots no Feature matched.

noSlotReason.description: Present only when the request named a connection and no slot may be filled on it: why nothing may attach there. Absent wherever the socket declares a slot. The set is closed.

oneOf.description: A Feature drew the connection, and an attachment is written only on a connection a component or the Release draws.
The socket is one the Component does not declare, so it declares no slot for a connection to fill.
The Component declares the socket and declares no slot on it.

ConnectionCandidatesResult.description: Which entities each socket on the entity may be wired to.

node.description: The entity whose sockets these are.

adHocSocketsAccepted.description: Whether a socket the entity's own definition does not pre-declare may still be authored.

sockets.description: Each socket and what may be wired into it.

InsertionPointResult.description: Where in the document a new entry under the named container belongs, and what a client needs in order to write it there: the point itself, whether a line break has to open the text, the container keys that are still missing, and the indentation each line takes.

file.description: The document.

container.description: The path through the document to the container.

positionEncoding.description: The encoding the positions in this answer are expressed in.

precededByLineBreak.description: Whether the text written at the position has to begin with a line break, because the position sits at the end of a line the document already carries. It is false only where the document carries nothing for the entry to follow.

missingContainerKeys.description: The container path's segments the document does not carry yet, outermost first. Each has to be written as a key of its own, indented one step further than the one before it, before the entry can go inside the innermost one. It is null where the whole path is already there.

entryIndent.description: The column the entry's own first line starts at, counted in spaces from the start of the line.

indentStep.description: How much further each nesting level is indented.

indentStepMeasured.description: Whether the step was measured from this document's own nesting. Where it is false the document exhibits no nesting to measure and the step is a fallback, so a client that would rather impose its own knows it is free to.

entryShape.description: The shape the container carries its entries in, which is what decides how the entry's own text is composed. It is read off the container the document already carries and is never inferred from what the container is called. The set is closed.

oneOf.description: The container is a block mapping, so an entry appended to it is a key and its value.
The container is a block sequence, so an entry appended to it is a dash and its value.
The document does not carry the container, or carries it with nothing in it, so which shape an entry takes is the client's to decide.

AttachmentContainerResult.description: Which document, and where in it, an attachment on the graph node, or on the connection the request named, belongs.

node.description: The graph node the attachment is for.

file.description: The document the attachment belongs in.

container.description: The path through that document to where it belongs.

ConnectionAtPositionResult.description: The connection whose entry the position falls inside, or why none is reported. Exactly one half is present: graphNode and connection together, or noConnectionReason alone. A position anywhere inside an entry — on its alias, its target or its attachments — is inside that entry, the innermost one where entries nest; a position on a socket's own key, above the entries written under it, is inside none.

graphNode.description: The id of the node whose component draws the connection, as the compiled graph keys it — the value the candidacy and container requests take as graphNode.

connection.description: The connection, by its socket and its alias, with document naming the document the position was read in — the value the candidacy and container requests take as connection.

noConnectionReason.description: Present only where no connection is reported: why. The set is closed.

oneOf.description: The position is on no entry an attachment is written in: neither a connection a component draws, written under its alias, nor a per-edge entry in the Release. A connection written as a list of targets, and one a Feature's own block draws, carry no such entry.
The position is on the Release's entry for a connection a Feature drew, and an attachment is written only on a connection a component or the Release draws.
The position is on an entry the Release writes for a connection the compiled graph does not carry.

ReleaseCandidatesResult.description: The Releases the workspace holds, and the links leading out of it, to directories and to files, that were not read for them.

lockfiles.description: The lockfile of each Release listed, keyed by the Release exactly as it is listed. Each is the file a pull writes for that Release and a build reads, so a client reads where it lives rather than working it out. Empty when the workspace holds no Release.

unreadLinkedDirs.description: Each link under the workspace root that leads to a directory outside it, named relative to the root where the link itself sits, in the order the workspace is searched. No directory outside the root is searched, so a Release reached only through one of these links is not in releases, and a client offering Releases can say why. Not named: a link to a directory inside the root, which is searched, or left out, where it actually sits; a link wherever a directory would be left out, whether by where it sits or by its name; and a link that cannot be resolved, because it leads nowhere or round a loop. Empty when the workspace holds none.

unreadLinkedFiles.description: Each link under the workspace root that is named like a YAML file, its own name ending in .yaml or .yml, and leads to a file outside the root, named relative to the root where the link itself sits, in the order the workspace is searched. Such a file is not read, so a Release reached only through one of these links is not in releases, and a client offering Releases can say why. Whether a file is a Release is not known without reading it, so each such link is named whatever the file holds. Not named: a link to a file the workspace configuration names as a Release, as build.authoring_release or as a key of workspace.releases, which is read and listed in releases at the link's own place; a link to a file inside the root, which is read; a link inside a directory the search leaves out; and a link that leads to no file, whether to a directory, which unreadLinkedDirs names where it leads out of the root, or nowhere, or round a loop. A workspace configuration file that is a link leading out of the workspace, its own .aggrega-config.yaml or the CI-owned overlay beside it, is named whether or not the search met it, after the links the search named: the workspace's configuration is then not read at all, this answer is read with nothing configured, so no Release the configuration names through a link is listed, and every request the configuration decides is refused for that workspace with the read hold's condition. Empty when the workspace holds none.

ActiveReleaseResult.description: Which Release a client should act on by default. A workspace pointing at no Release is an ordinary state rather than a failure, so it is reported here with an account of how the choice was attempted rather than raised as an error.

release.description: The Release that was settled on, or empty where none was.

lockfile.description: The lockfile of the Release that was settled on: the file a pull writes for it and a build reads. Absent where no Release was settled on.

reason.description: Why no Release was settled on.

trace.description: Each step of the choice and what it found, so a caller can see which one would have settled it.

EditDocumentResult.description: What the edit wrote, and where. After a write the daemon's reading of the document is dropped, so the next answer about it is computed from the bytes the edit produced.

file.description: The document that was edited.

container.description: The path through the document to where the edit landed.

createdContainers.description: The containers the edit had to create on the way.

content.description: The composed document, for a request that asked to be shown the result rather than have it written.

EffectiveConfigurationResult.description: The configuration the workspace resolved, and which document each setting came from.

layers.description: The configuration documents that were merged, in the order they were merged.

settings.description: Each resolved setting and where it came from.

ConfigInitResult.description: What seeding a configuration wrote, where, and what it read from the registry.

host.description: The registry the configuration was seeded for.

written.description: Whether the document was written, as against handed back for the caller to place.

existed.description: Present and true when the document was already there, so the registry entry was merged into it rather than a new document created. Only a request sending force proceeds over an existing document, so it is absent from every answer to one that did not.

content.description: The document's text, for a request that asked to be shown it rather than have it written.

ConfigCaptureResult.description: What freezing the resolved configuration wrote into this workspace's own document.

configFile.description: The document that was written. It is always this workspace's own, since the whole purpose is to make one workspace self-contained.

sockets.description: Each socket that was frozen, with its attachments.

catalogDirs.description: The catalog directories that were frozen.

ImportResult.description: What converting a foreign source produced, and what it could not convert.

format.description: The source format that was converted.

outputDir.description: The directory every path in the answer is relative to, and the one the files were written into.

written.description: Each file that reached disk, in the order written: the drafts, then the record of what the import wrote. Under sync, only the drafts the sync changed and the record where it changed. Empty under dryRun.

files.description: Each file the request writes, with its text, under dryRun and without it: every draft, then the record of what the import wrote. Under sync, each draft the sync changes, with its new text, then the record where that changes too, so a sync in step answers an empty list.

drift.description: Each part a sync brought up to date with the source, or under dryRun would, in the order the draft names them; a drafted file the sync deletes is one of them, removed with no keys. An empty list for a request that is not a sync, for a sync in step, and for a sync whose conversion stopped, which writes nothing.

decisions.description: How the importer mapped each source node, in the importer's order and exactly as it reported it: what tells you where the conversion guessed. Carried under both deliveries and whether or not the conversion stopped, and an empty list for an importer that reports none.

owed.description: Each value the drafts still leave empty that no source could supply and no answer did, in the order the drafts are written — the values the warning findings name. Every answer carries it, an empty list where the drafts owe nothing.

halted.description: Whether the conversion stopped rather than finishing with findings.

ScaffoldEntityResult.description: The drafted starter document, the list of runnable examples, or the example written — each form answering with its own fields and leaving the others absent.

kind.description: The entity kind that was drafted. Present on a draft.

skeleton.description: The drafted document's text. Present on a draft.

examples.description: Every runnable example the documentation publishes, each once, in name order. Present on a list that found any.

example.description: The example that was written. Present on a write.

dir.description: The directory the example was written into, relative to the workspace root, as the request named it or, where it named none, as the example's name. Present on a write.

files.description: Each file written, relative to dir and slash-separated, in the order the documentation carries them. Present on a write.

next.description: The commands the example's page gives for building it, line by line as the page writes them, comments included: the first shell block under its Build heading. Absent where the page gives none.

version.description: The version of the documentation the example was read from: the binary's own where one is published for it, otherwise the newest published before it. Present on a write.

ScaffoldExample.description: One runnable example the documentation publishes.

name.description: The example's name, which a request sends as example to write it.

level.description: The level the example's page declares for it.

summary.description: The first sentence of the example's page.

LintResult.description: What the convention check found, counted by severity and listed per document. A whole-catalog check that ran once for each Release also carries passes; the counts and files then cover every pass together.

entity.description: The one entity that was checked, where the request named one.

release.description: The Release whose closure was checked, where the request named one.

checked.description: How many documents were checked. Where the check ran once for each Release, the sum over the passes: a document two passes read is counted in each.

findings.description: How many findings there are in total.

errors.description: How many of them are errors.

warnings.description: How many of them are warnings.

infos.description: How many of them are informational.

halted.description: Whether the check stopped rather than finishing with findings.

passes.description: The whole-catalog check one pass at a time, present only where it ran once for each Release because the workspace names Releases under workspace.releases. Each pass says which Releases its findings were found for. Absent for a workspace that names none, which is checked once over its own directories, and for a check of one entity or of a Release's closure.

LintPass.description: One pass of a whole-catalog convention check in a workspace that gives its Releases catalog directories of their own: the Releases it was run for, the directories it read, and what it found there.

releases.description: The Releases the pass was run for, each as a path relative to the workspace root. Releases that read the same catalog directories share one pass.

catalogDirs.description: The catalog directories the pass read, in the order they are searched, each relative to the workspace root where it lies inside it. Empty where its Releases read no catalog directory, so the pass checked nothing and failed none of the others.

checked.description: How many documents the pass checked.

findings.description: How many findings the pass found.

errors.description: How many of them are errors.

warnings.description: How many of them are warnings.

infos.description: How many of them are informational.

PluginAddResult.description: What attaching a plugin wrote, where, and which version it pinned.

type.description: The socket the plugin was attached to.

identity.description: The identity the attachment resolved to.

uri.description: The reference the attachment resolves from.

capability.description: The capability the attachment is for.

written.description: Whether the configuration document was written, as against handed back for the caller to place.

content.description: The configuration document's text, for a request that asked to be shown it rather than have it written.

withdrawn.description: True when the query named the version that was pinned and a retraction this workspace trusts has withdrawn that version. A named version is pinned all the same, because naming it is the override. Absent otherwise, and absence does not mean the version is not withdrawn: where the withdrawal markers of a named version could not be read, retraction.unscreened says why, and with no version named, the latest published version is chosen and retraction reports what the withdrawal check concluded about that choice.

PluginRemoveResult.description: What detaching a plugin wrote, and where.

type.description: The socket the plugin was attached to.

PluginSyncResult.description: What aligning a Plugin entity's machine-owned records with its module changed.

entity.description: The Plugin entity document that was aligned.

hostFunctions.description: The host functions the module declares it needs.

changed.description: Whether anything in the document actually moved.

PluginGenCatalogResult.description: The catalog documents a generation produced.

documents.description: Each generated document and its text.

notices.description: Anything the generation wants the caller to know.

dryRun.description: Whether the documents were handed back rather than written.

ExplainErrorResult.description: What the compiler declares about a condition, and the published passages teaching the authoring fix.

message.description: What the condition says when it is raised.

entries.description: The published passages teaching the fix.

reference.description: The published address at which the condition is explained.

note.description: Why the published passages are missing, where they could not be acquired. What the binary itself declares is still answered.

GetSchemaResult.description: A kind's schema, or — where the request named none — which kinds can be named. The two widths ride on one answer rather than on two methods, because 'what may I name' and 'which of those does an author write documents of' are the same question at two widths, and two answers would have to be kept in agreement.

kind.description: The kind the schema is for.

schema.description: The schema itself, carried through as the binary holds it.

kinds.description: Every token this binary answers to.

entityKinds.description: The narrower set an author writes a document of, each pairing the token a request names with the kind the document's own header declares.

SkillsInstallResult.description: What installing the assistant skill wrote, and where.

installed.description: Each skill folder written, in the order the request named the assistants. Assistants reading one shared folder share one entry, because the skill is written there once.

SkillsInstalledFolder.description: One skill folder an installation wrote.

agents.description: The identifiers of the named assistants that read this folder, in the order the request named them.

folder.description: The skill's folder, as an absolute path.

replaced.description: Whether a copy carrying the comment line every written copy of the skill carries — one an earlier installation wrote, or one taken from the published skills repository — was there and has been replaced. A file there without that line is refused rather than replaced.

SkillsListResult.description: The skills the binary ships and every assistant an installation can write them for. Nothing is written and nothing is reached.

skills.description: Each skill the binary ships, in a fixed order.

agents.description: Each assistant an installation knows a skill folder for, ordered by identifier.

name.description: The skill's name, which is also the name of the folder an installation writes.

description.description: When an assistant uses the skill, as the skill itself declares it.

SkillsListedAgent.description: One assistant an installation can write a skill for, with the two folders it reads skills from.

id.description: The identifier a request names the assistant by.

projectFolder.description: The folder, relative to a project's root and separated by slashes, that the assistant reads a project's skills from. A project installation writes the skill's folder inside it, in the workspace the request names.

userFolder.description: The folder, relative to the home directory and separated by slashes, that the assistant reads the user's own skills from in every project. An installation with global writes the skill's folder inside it.
